Also in the destruction of Jerusalem, most unexpected by the Jews, who to the last deceived themselves with the expectation that Messiah would suddenly appear as a temporal Saviour. Compare the use of "suddenly" in <reference osisRef="Num.12.4-Num.12.10">Nu 12:4-10</reference>, where He appeared in wrath.<div eID="gen25044" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25045" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">messenger of the covenant--</hi>namely, of the ancient covenant with Israel (<reference osisRef="Isa.63.9">Is 63:9</reference>) and Abraham, in which the promise to the Gentiles is ultimately included (<reference osisRef="Gal.4.16">Ga 4:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gal.4.17">17</reference>). The gospel at the first advent began with Israel, then embraced the Gentile world: so also it shall be at the second advent. All the manifestations of God in the Old Testament, the Shekinah and human appearances, were made in the person of the Divine Son (<reference osisRef="Exod.23.20">Ex 23:20</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.23.21">21</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.11.26">He 11:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.12.26">12:26</reference>). He was the messenger of the old covenant, as well as of the new. <div eID="gen25045" type="x-p"/>
entries.c941ee9e8bfc0ecc61eb29595c571b348132c63f: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13246"/><div sID="gen25046" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13246"/>2. (Mal 4:1; <reference osisRef="Rev.6.16">Re 6:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.6.17">17</reference>). The Messiah would come, not, as they expected, to flatter the theocratic nation's prejudices, but to subject their principles to the fiery test of His heart-searching truth (<reference osisRef="Matt.3.10-Matt.3.12">Mt 3:10-12</reference>), and to destroy Jerusalem and the theocracy after they had rejected Him. His mission is here regarded as a whole from the first to the second advent: the process of refining and separating the godly from the ungodly beginning during Christ's stay on earth, going on ever since, and about to continue till the final separation (<reference osisRef="Matt.25.31-Matt.25.46">Mt 25:31-46</reference>). The refining process, whereby a third of the Jews is refined as silver of its dross, while two-thirds perish, is described, <reference osisRef="Zech.13.8">Zec 13:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.13.9">9</reference> (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.1.25">Is 1:25</reference>). <div eID="gen25046" type="x-p"/>
entries.df0eb4faa067974fe402b88a458eb4e195b21983: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13247"/><div sID="gen25047" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13247"/><hi type="bold">3. sit--</hi>The purifier sits before the crucible, fixing his eye on the metal, and taking care that the fire be not too hot, and keeping the metal in, only until he knows the dross to be completely removed by his seeing his own image reflected (<reference osisRef="Rom.8.29">Ro 8:29</reference>) in the glowing mass. So the Lord in the case of His elect (<reference osisRef="Job.23.10">Job 23:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.66.10">Psa 66:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Prov.17.3">Pr 17:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.48.10">Is 48:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.12.10">He 12:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Pet.1.7">1Pe 1:7</reference>). He will sit down to the work, not perfunctorily, but with patient love and unflinching justice. The Angel of the Covenant, as in leading His people out of Egypt by the pillar of cloud and fire, has an aspect of terror to His foes, of love to His friends. The same separating process goes on in the world as in each Christian. When the godly are completely separated from the ungodly, the world will end. When the dross is taken from the gold of the Christian, he will be for ever delivered from the furnace of trial. The purer the gold, the hotter the fire now; the whiter the garment, the harder the washing [Moore].<div eID="gen25047" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25048" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">purify ... sons of Levi--</hi>of the sins specified above. The very Levites, the ministers of God, then needed cleansing, so universal was the depravity.<div eID="gen25048" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25049" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">that they may offer ... in righteousness--</hi>as originally (Mal 2:6), not as latterly (Mal 1:7-14). So believers, the spiritual priesthood (<reference osisRef="1Pet.2.5">1Pe 2:5</reference>). <div eID="gen25049" type="x-p"/>
entries.22e283d161624fb713e88258dc8ace7f02479770: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13248"/><div sID="gen25050" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13248"/><hi type="bold">4. as in the days of old--</hi>(Mal 1:11; <reference osisRef="2Cor.5.6">2:5, 6</reference>). The "offering" (Mincha, Hebrew) is not expiatory, but prayer, thanksgiving, and self-dedication (<reference osisRef="Rom.12.1">Ro 12:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.13.15">He 13:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Pet.2.5">1Pe 2:5</reference>). <div eID="gen25050" type="x-p"/>
entries.79189f282a9c04eeab32c18e0ea95a595d78c102: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13249"/><div sID="gen25051" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13249"/><hi type="bold">5. I ... come near ... to judgment--</hi>I whom ye challenged, saying, "Where is the God of judgment?" (Mal 2:17). I whom ye think far off, and to be slow in judgment, am "near," and will come as a "swift witness"; not only a judge, but also an eye-witness against sorcerers; for Mine eyes see every sin, though ye think I take no heed. Earthly judges need witnesses to enable them to decide aright: I alone need none (<reference osisRef="Ps.10.11">Psa 10:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.73.11">73:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.94.7">94:7</reference>, &c.).<div eID="gen25051" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25052" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sorcerers--</hi>a sin into which the Jews were led in connection with their foreign idolatrous wives. The Jews of Christ's time also practised sorcery (<reference osisRef="Acts.8.9">Ac 8:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.13.6">13:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gal.5.20">Ga 5:20</reference>; Josephus [Antiquities, 20.6; Wars of the Jews, 2.12.23]). It shall be a characteristic of the last Antichristian confederacy, about to be consumed by the brightness of Christ's Coming (<reference osisRef="Matt.24.24">Mt 24:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Thess.2.9">2Th 2:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.13.13">Re 13:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.13.14">14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.16.13">16:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.16.14">14</reference>; also <reference osisRef="Rev.9.21">Re 9:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.18.23">18:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.21.8">21:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.22.15">22:15</reference>). Romanism has practised it; an order of exorcists exists in that Church.<div eID="gen25052" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25053" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">adulterers--</hi>(Mal 2:15, 16).<div eID="gen25053" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25054" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">fear not me--</hi>the source of all sins. <div eID="gen25054" type="x-p"/>
entries.07aa5e86ef013513d379146d16fe53622dff7d8f: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13250"/><div sID="gen25055" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13250"/><hi type="bold">6. the Lord--</hi>Jehovah: a name implying His immutable faithfulness in fulfilling His promises: the covenant name of God to the Jews (<reference osisRef="Exod.6.3">Ex 6:3</reference>), called here "the sons of Jacob," in reference to God's covenant with that patriarch.<div eID="gen25055" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25056" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I change not--</hi>Ye are mistaken in inferring that, because I have not yet executed judgment on the wicked, I am changed from what I once was, namely, a God of judgment.<div eID="gen25056" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25057" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">therefore ye ... are not consumed--</hi>Ye yourselves being "not consumed," as ye have long ago deserved, are a signal proof of My unchangeableness. <reference osisRef="Rom.11.29">Ro 11:29</reference>: compare the whole chapter, in which God's mercy in store for Israel is made wholly to flow from God's unchanging faithfulness to His own covenant of love. So here, as is implied by the phrase "sons of Jacob" (<reference osisRef="Gen.28.13">Ge 28:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gen.35.12">35:12</reference>). They are spared because I am Jehovah, and they sons of Jacob; while I spare them, I will also punish them; and while I punish them, I will not wholly consume them. The unchangeableness of God is the sheet-anchor of the Church. The perseverance of the saints is guaranteed, not by their unchangeable love to God, but by His unchangeable love to them, and His eternal purpose and promise in Christ Jesus [Moore]. He upbraids their ingratitude that they turn His very long-suffering (<reference osisRef="Lam.3.22">La 3:22</reference>) into a ground for skeptical denial of His coming as a Judge at all (<reference osisRef="Ps.50.1">Psa 50:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.3.4">3, 4</reference>, 21; <reference osisRef="Eccl.8.11">Ec 8:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Eccl.8.12">12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.57.11">Is 57:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.2.4-Rom.2.10">Ro 2:4-10</reference>). <div eID="gen25057" type="x-p"/>
entries.4e125afd615f4de0e27f7ac7ef27a4acb2c0d7cf: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13251"/><div sID="gen25058" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13251"/>7-12. Reproof for the non-payment of tithes and offerings, which is the cause of their national calamities, and promise of prosperity on their paying them.<div eID="gen25058" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25059" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from ... days of your fathers--</hi>Ye live as your fathers did when they brought on themselves the Babylonian captivity, and ye wish to follow in their steps. This shows that nothing but God's unchanging long-suffering had prevented their being long ago "consumed" (Mal 3:6).<div eID="gen25059" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25060" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Return unto me--</hi>in penitence.<div eID="gen25060" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25061" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I will return unto you--</hi>in blessings.<div eID="gen25061" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25062" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Wherein, &c.--</hi>(Mal 3:16). The same insensibility to their guilt continues: they speak in the tone of injured innocence, as if God calumniated them. <div eID="gen25062" type="x-p"/>
entries.30491156beb8638087cda488a1fafde8d549a122: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13257"/><div sID="gen25075" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13257"/>13-18. He notices the complaint of the Jews that it is of no profit to serve Jehovah, for that the ungodly proud are happy; and declares He will soon bring the day when it shall be known that He puts an everlasting distinction between the godly and the ungodly.<div eID="gen25075" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25076" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">words ... stout--</hi>Hebrew, "hard"; so "the hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against Him" (Jude 15) [Henderson].<div eID="gen25076" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25077" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">have we spoken--</hi>The Hebrew expresses at once their assiduity and habit of speaking against God [Vatablus]. The niphal form of the verb implies that these things were said, not directly to God, but of God, to one another (<reference osisRef="Ezek.33.20">Eze 33:20</reference>) [Moore]. <div eID="gen25077" type="x-p"/>

entries.b47447db1a5e9e485acbb6b45aa8b98f799f1038: <div eID="gen35896" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen35897" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen35898" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen35898" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen35897" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen35899" type="x-p"/> In allusion to the custom of sending pioneers to prepare the way for the march of an eastern monarch, the coming of Christ's forerunner is described, and then the coming of Christ himself, <reference osisRef="Mal.3.1">Mal 3:1</reference>; with the terrible judgments which were to accompany that event, in order to refine and purify his people and his priests, <reference osisRef="Mal.3.2-Mal.3.6">Mal 3:2-6</reference>. The following verses reprehend them for withholding the legal tithes and offerings, with large promises in case of their repentance and amendments, <reference osisRef="Mal.3.7-Mal.3.12">Mal 3:7-12</reference>. The prophet expostulates with the people for their hard and profane speeches against the conduct of Providence, and declares God will one day make a fearful and final distinction between the righteous and the wicked, whose different characters are in the mean time carefully recorded, <reference osisRef="Mal.3.13-Mal.3.18">Mal 3:13-18</reference>. <div eID="gen35899" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35900" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen35900" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35901" type="x-p"/> Behold, I will send my messenger - מלאכי Malachi, the very name of the prophet. But this speaks of John the Baptist. I, the Messiah, the Seed of God, mentioned above, will send my messenger, John the Baptist. <div eID="gen35901" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35902" type="x-p"/> He shall prepare the way - Be as a pioneer before me; a corrector of civil abuses, and a preacher of righteousness. <div eID="gen35902" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35903" type="x-p"/> And the Lord, whom ye seek - The Messiah, whom ye expect, from the account given by the prophet Daniel, in his seventy weeks, <reference osisRef="Dan.9.24">Dan 9:24</reference>. <div eID="gen35903" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35904" type="x-p"/> Shall suddenly come to his temple - Shall soon be presented before the Lord in his temple; cleanse it from its defilement, and fill it with his teaching and his glory. <div eID="gen35904" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35905" type="x-p"/> The Messenger of the covenant - He that comes to fulfill the great design, in reference to the covenant made with Abram, that in his seed all the families of the earth should be blessed. See the parallel texts in the margin, and the notes on them.
entries.81a0dc4c3f868eb5a05b1c444faa1e94a7053e62: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen35905" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35906" type="x-p"/> But who may abide the day of his coming? - Only they who shall believe on his name; for they that will not, shall be blinded, and the unbelieving nations shall be destroyed by the Romans. <div eID="gen35906" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35907" type="x-p"/> Like fuller's soap - כברית keborith, from ברר barar, to cleanse, any thing that deterges. Kali, or fern ashes, or such things. I doubt whether the composition which we call soap, was known in ancient times.
entries.5171203b1b4a272a8618dbdca74b63c6554168cf: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen35907" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35908" type="x-p"/> He shall sit as a refiner - Alluding to the case of a refiner of metals, sitting at his fire; increasing it when he sees necessary, and watching the process of his work. <div eID="gen35908" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35909" type="x-p"/> The sons of Levi - Those who minister in their stead under the New covenant, for the Old Levitical institutions shall be abolished; yet, under the preaching of our Lord, a great number of the priests became obedient to the faith, <reference osisRef="Act.6.7">Act 6:7</reference>; and, as to the others that did not believe, this great Refiner threw them as dross into the Roman fire, that consumed both Jerusalem and the temple.
entries.609ec8e1c1e80a7f2219df94134f06b9705853c5: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen35909" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35910" type="x-p"/> I will come near to you to judgment - And what fearful cases does he get to judge! Sorcerers, adulterers, false swearers, defrauders of the wages of the hireling, oppressors of widows and orphans, and perverters of the stranger and such as do not fear the Lord: a horrible crew; and the land at that time was full of them. Several were converted under the preaching of Christ and his apostles, and the rest the Romans destroyed or carried into captivity.
entries.33069a7b56e950346d6f05a2b3be6aa99240815d: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen35910" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35911" type="x-p"/> I am the Lord, I change not - The new dispensation of grace and goodness, which is now about to be introduced, is not the effect of any change in my counsels; it is, on the contrary, the fulfillment of my everlasting purposes; as is also the throwing aside of the Mosaic ritual, which was only intended to introduce the great and glorious Gospel of my Son. <div eID="gen35911" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35912" type="x-p"/> And because of this ancient covenant, ye Jews are not totally consumed; but ye are now, and shall be still, preserved as a distinct people - monuments both of my justice and mercy.
entries.50a28bdda16cb1f55170fdc9d6339803724e1317: <hi type="bold">Verse 7</hi> <div eID="gen35912" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35913" type="x-p"/> Gone away from mine ordinances - Never acting according to their spirit and design. <div eID="gen35913" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35914" type="x-p"/> Return unto me - There is still space to repent. <div eID="gen35914" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35915" type="x-p"/> Wherein shall we return? - Their consciences were seared, and they knew not that they were sinners.
entries.7782d81cf37819abb0917c5e3e57e66ebdcda327: <hi type="bold">Verse 8</hi> <div eID="gen35915" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35916" type="x-p"/> Will a man rob God? - Here is one point on which ye are guilty; ye withhold the tithes and offerings from the temple of God, so that the Divine worship is neglected.
entries.5fb333ce310e9ff69e45670c1388909053380b21: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen35916" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35917" type="x-p"/> Ye are cursed with a curse - The whole nation is under my displeasure. The curse of God is upon you.
entries.ebfadef3a53e4284bda7995eac1b2153aa4ad072: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen35917" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35918" type="x-p"/> Bring ye all the tithes - They had so withheld these that the priests had not food enough to support life, and the sacred service was interrupted. See <reference osisRef="Neh.13.10">Neh 13:10</reference>. <div eID="gen35918" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35919" type="x-p"/> And prove me now herewith - What ye give to God shall never lessen your store. Give as ye should, and see whether I will not so increase your store by opening the windows of heaven - giving you rain and fruitful seasons - that your barns and granaries shall not be able to contain the abundance of your harvests and vintage.
entries.cbc690c931c6f7207de646bfe05a8fa95f1027f2: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen35919" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35920" type="x-p"/> I wilt rebuke the devourer - The locusts, etc., shall not come on your crops; and those that are in the country I will disperse and destroy. <div eID="gen35920" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35921" type="x-p"/> Neither shall your vine cast her fruit - Every blossom shall bear fruit, and every bunch of grapes come to maturity.
entries.2014d678830ee58603a06c2d5084401e7b474768: <hi type="bold">Verse 12</hi> <div eID="gen35921" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35922" type="x-p"/> All nations shall call you blessed - They shall see that a peculiar blessing of God rests upon you, and your land shall be delightsome; like Paradise, the garden of the Lord.
entries.1fc76a7a40f686c39d0768de2da8b9211ca68d2d: <hi type="bold">Verse 13</hi> <div eID="gen35922" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35923" type="x-p"/> Your words have been stout against me - He speaks here to open infidels and revilers. <div eID="gen35923" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35924" type="x-p"/> What have we spoken - They are ready either to deny the whole, or impudently to maintain and defend what they had spoken!
entries.d654d19e6b5502761bd31a1e721384014be02156: <hi type="bold">Verse 14</hi> <div eID="gen35924" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35925" type="x-p"/> Ye have said, It is vain to serve God - They strove to destroy the Divine worship; they asserted that it was vanity; that, if they performed acts of worship, they should be nothing the better; and if they abstained, they should be nothing the worse. This was their teaching to the people. <div eID="gen35925" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35926" type="x-p"/> Walked mournfully - Even repentance they have declared to be useless. This was a high pitch of ungodliness; but see what follows; behold the general conclusions of these reprobates: -
entries.7ac2f3348f4ece5c341d5f615e2acfde7fb75758: <hi type="bold">Verse 15</hi> <div eID="gen35926" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35927" type="x-p"/> And now we call the proud happy - Proud and insolent men are the only happy people, for they domineer everywhere, and none dares to resist them. <div eID="gen35927" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35928" type="x-p"/> They that work wickedness are set up - The humble and holy are depressed and miserable; the proud and wicked are in places of trust and profit. Too often it is so. <div eID="gen35928" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35929" type="x-p"/> They that tempt God are even delivered - Even those who despise God, and insult his justice and providence, are preserved in and from dangers; while the righteous fall by them.
entries.4bb1d29bd4f0b3f7fd9bfb830317001804999282: <hi type="bold">Verse 16</hi> <div eID="gen35929" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35930" type="x-p"/> They that feared the Lord - There were a few godly in the land, who, hearing the language and seeing the profligacy of the rebels above, concluded that some signal mark of God's vengeance must fall upon them; they, therefore, as the corruption increased, cleaved the closer to their Maker. There are three characteristics given of this people, viz.: - <div eID="gen35930" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35931" type="x-p"/> 1. They feared the Lord. They had that reverence for Jehovah that caused them to depart from evil, and to keep his ordinances. <div eID="gen35931" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35932" type="x-p"/> 2. They spake often one to another. They kept up the communion of saints. By mutual exhortation they strengthened each other's hands in the Lord. <div eID="gen35932" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35933" type="x-p"/> 3. They thought on his name. His name was sacred to them; it was a fruitful source of profound and edifying meditation. The name of God is God himself in the plenitude of his power, omniscience, justice, goodness, mercy, and truth. What a source for thinking and contemplation! See how God treats such persons: The Lord hearkened to their conversation, heard the meditations of their hearts; and so approved of the whole that a book of remembrance was written before the Lord - all their names were carefully registered in heaven. Here is an allusion to records kept by kings, <reference osisRef="Est.6.1">Est 6:1</reference>, of such as had performed signal services, and who should be the first to be rewarded.
entries.282b122307a74d70bf85f89455a56a075dbf4a1d: <hi type="bold">Verse 17</hi> <div eID="gen35933" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35934" type="x-p"/> They shall be mine - I will acknowledge them as my subjects and followers; in the day, especially, when I come to punish the wicked and reward the righteous. <div eID="gen35934" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35935" type="x-p"/> When I make up my jewels - סגלה segullah, my peculium, my proper treasure; that which is a man's own, and most prized by him. Not jewels; for in no part of the Bible does the word mean a gem or precious stone of any kind. The interpretations frequently given of the word in this verse, comparing saints to jewels, are forced and false. <div eID="gen35935" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35936" type="x-p"/> I will spare them - When I come to visit the wicked, I will take care of them. I will act towards them as a tender father would act towards his most loving and obedient son.
entries.66766f6caa9a4f1f51a03b64263865742fc95807: <hi type="bold">Verse 18</hi> <div eID="gen35936" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35937" type="x-p"/> Then shall ye return - To your senses, when perhaps too late; and discern - see the difference which God makes, between the righteous and the wicked, which will be most marked and awful. <div eID="gen35937" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35938" type="x-p"/> Between him that serveth God - Your obedience to whom, ye said, would be unprofitable to you. <div eID="gen35938" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35939" type="x-p"/> And hits that serveth him not - Of whom ye said, his disobedience would be no prejudice to him. You will find the former received into the kingdom of glory; and the latter, with yourselves, thrust down into the bitter pains of an eternal death. Reader, ponder these things. <div eID="gen35939" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35940" type="x-p"/> In the great day of the Lord, at least, if not long before, it will be fully discovered who have been the truly wise people; those who took up their cross and followed Christ; or those who satisfied the flesh, with its affections and desires, following a multitude to do evil.  <chapter eID="Mal.3"/> <div eID="gen35940" type="x-p"/>

entries.dad69caa31906583807f78d20fedcb34f189f8cc: Mal 3:1 <div eID="gen16965" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16966" type="x-p"/> Coming of the Lord to judgment. Mal 3:1. <hi type="italic">“Behold, I send my messenger, that he may prepare the way before me; and the Lord, whom ye seek, will suddenly come to His temple, and the angel of the covenant, whom ye desire; behold he comes, saith Jehovah of hosts.” </hi> To the question, Where is or remains the God of judgment? the Lord Himself replies that He will suddenly come to His temple, but that before His coming He will send a messenger to prepare the way for Him. The announcement of this messenger rests upon the prophecy in Isa 40:3., as the expression וּפנּה דרך, which is borrowed from that passage, clearly shows. The person whose voice Isaiah heard calling to make the way of Jehovah in the desert, that the glory of the Lord might be revealed to all flesh, is here described as מלאך, whom Jehovah will send before Him, i.e., before His coming. This <hi type="italic">maleâkh</hi> is not a heavenly messenger, or spiritual being (Rashi, Kimchi), nor the angel of Jehovah κατ ̓ ἐξοχήν, who is mentioned afterwards and called <hi type="italic">maleakh habberı̄th</hi>, but an earthly messenger of the Lord, and indeed the same who is called the prophet Elijah in Mal 4:5, and therefore not “an ideal person, viz., the whole choir of divine messengers, who are to prepare the way for the coming of salvation, and open the door for the future grace” (Hengst.), but a concrete personality - a messenger who was really sent to the nation in John the Baptist immediately before the coming of the Lord. The idea view is precluded not only by the historical fact, that not a single prophet arose in Israel during the whole period between Malachi and John, but also by the context of the passage before us, according to which the sending of the messenger was to take place immediately before the coming of the Lord to His temple. It is true that in Mal 2:7 the priest is also called a messenger of Jehovah; but the expression הנני שׁלח (behold I send) prevents our understanding the term <hi type="italic">maleâkh</hi> as referring to the priests, or even as including them, inasmuch as “sending” would not apply to the priests as the standing mediators between the Lord and His people. Moreover, it was because the priests did not fulfil their duty as the ordinary ambassadors of God that the Lord was about to send an extraordinary messenger. Preparing the way (פּנה דרך, an expression peculiar to Isaiah: compare <reference osisRef="Isa.40.3">Isa 40:3</reference>; also, <reference osisRef="Isa.57.14">Isa 57:14</reference> and <reference osisRef="Isa.62.10">Isa 62:10</reference>), by clearing away the impediments lying in the road, denotes the removal of all that retards the coming of the Lord to His people, i.e., the taking away of enmity to God and of ungodliness by the preaching of repentance and the conversion of sinners. The announcement of this messenger therefore implied, that the nation in its existing moral condition was not yet prepared for the reception of the Lord, and therefore had no ground for murmuring at the delay of the manifestation of the divine glory, but ought rather to murmur at its own sin and estrangement from God. When the way shall have been prepared, the Lord will suddenly come. פּתאם, not <hi type="italic">statim</hi>, immediately (Jerome), but unexpectedly. “This suddenness is repeated in all the acts and judgments of the Lord. The Lord of glory always comes as a thief in the night to those who sleep in their sins” (Schmieder). “The Lord” (<hi type="italic">hâ'âdōn</hi>) is God; this is evident both from the fact that He comes to <hi type="italic">His</hi> temple, i.e., the temple of Jehovah, and also from the relative clause “whom ye seek,” which points back to the question, “Where is the God of judgment?” (Mal 2:17). The Lord comes to His temple (<hi type="italic">hēkhâl</hi>, lit., palace) as the God-king of Israel, to dwell therein for ever (cf. <reference osisRef="Ezek.43.7">Eze 43:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.37.26-Ezek.37.27">Eze 37:26-27</reference>). And He comes as the angel of the covenant, for whom the people are longing. The identity of the angel of the covenant with the “Lord” (<hi type="italic">hâ'âdōn</hi>) is placed beyond the reach of doubt by the parallelism of the clauses, and the notion is thereby refuted that the “covenant angel” is identical with the person previously mentioned as מלאכי (Hitzig, Maurer, etc.). This identity does not indeed exclude a distinction of person; but it does exclude a difference between the two, or the opinion that the angel of the covenant is that mediator whom Isaiah had promised (<reference osisRef="Isa.42.6">Isa 42:6</reference>) as the antitype of Moses, and the mediator of a new, perfect, and eternally-enduring covenant relation between God and Israel (Hofmann, <hi type="italic">Schriftbeweis</hi>, i. p. 183). For it was not for a second Moses that the people were longing, or for a mediator of the new covenant, but for the coming of God to judgment. The coming of the Lord to His temple is represented as a coming of the covenant angel, with reference to the fact that Jehovah had in the olden time revealed His glory in His <hi type="italic">Maleakh</hi> in a manner perceptible to the senses, and that in this mode of revelation He had not only redeemed Israel out of the hand of Egypt (Exo 3:6.), gone before the army of Israel (<reference osisRef="Exod.14.19">Exo 14:19</reference>), and led Israel through the desert to Canaan (Exo 23:20., Exo 33:14.), but had also filled the temple with His glory. The covenant, in relation to which the <hi type="italic">Maleakh</hi>, who is of one essence with Jehovah, is here called the angel of the covenant, is not the new covenant promised in Jer 31:31., but the covenant of Jehovah with Israel, according to which Jehovah dwells in the midst of Israel, and manifests His gracious presence by blessing the righteous and punishing the ungodly (cf. <reference osisRef="Exod.25.8">Exo 25:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.25.11-Lev.25.12">Lev 25:11-12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.4.24">Deu 4:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.33.14">Isa 33:14</reference>): (Koehler). The words “Behold he (the covenant angel) cometh” serve to confirm the assurance, and are still further strengthened by אמר יי צ (saith Jehovah of hosts). This promise was fulfilled in the coming of Christ, in whom the angel of the covenant, the Logos, became flesh, and in the sending of John the Baptist, who prepared the way for Him. (See also at Mal 4:6)
entries.c68734ba10dab57e7d4d6f0de8cc7b229fdf0127: Mal 3:2-4 <div eID="gen16966" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16967" type="x-p"/> With the coming of the Lord the judgment will also begin; not the judgment upon the heathen, however, for which the ungodly nation was longing, but the judgment upon the godless members of the covenant nation. Mal 3:2. <hi type="italic">“And who endures the day of His coming? and who can stand at His appearing? for He is like the smelter’s fire, and like washers’ lye:</hi> Mal 3:3. <hi type="italic">And will sit smelting and purifying silver, and will purify the children of Levi, and refine like gold and silver, that they may be offering to Jehovah His sacrifice in righteousness.</hi> Mal 3:4. <hi type="italic">And the sacrifice of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasant, as in the days of the olden time, and as in the years of the past.” </hi> The question “who endures the day” has a negative meaning, like מי in <reference osisRef="Isa.53.1">Isa 53:1</reference> : no one endures it (for the fact itself compare <reference osisRef="Joel.2.11">Joe 2:11</reference>). The prophet is speaking to the ungodly. The second clause is synonymous. עמד, to remain standing, in contrast with falling, or sinking under the burden of the judgment. The reason for this is given in the second hemistich. The Lord when He comes will be like a smelter’s fire, which burns out all the corrupt ingredients that are mixed with the gold and silver (cf. Zec 13:9), and like the lye or alkaline salt by which clothes are cleansed from dirt (cf. <reference osisRef="Isa.4.4">Isa 4:4</reference>). The double figure has but one meaning; hence only the first figure is carried out in Mal 3:3, a somewhat different turn being given to it, since the Lord is no longer compared to the fire, but represented as a smelter. As a smelter purifies gold and silver from the dross adhering to it, so will the Lord refine the sons of Levi, by whom the priests are principally intended. The <hi type="italic">yâshabh</hi> (sit) serves as a pictorial description, like <hi type="italic">‛âmad</hi> (stand) in Mic 5:3. The participles <hi type="italic">metsârēph</hi> and <hi type="italic">metahēr</hi> describe the capacity in which He sits, viz., as a smelter and purifier of silver. זקּק: to strain, or filter; a term transferred to metals, because in smelting the pure metal is allowed to flow off, so that the earthy ingredients are left in the crucible (<reference osisRef="Ps.12.7">Psa 12:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.28.1">Job 28:1</reference>, etc.). The fact that the sons of Levi are named, as the object of the refining action of the Lord, is to be explained from what is mentioned in Mal 1:6. concerning their degeneracy. Since they, the supporters and promoters of the religious life of the nation, were quite corrupt, the renovation of the national life must begin with their purification. This purification, however, does not consist merely in the fact, that the individuals who are displeasing to God will be cut off from among them (Koehler), nor merely in their being cleansed from the sins and crimes adhering to them (Hitzig), but in both, so that those who are corrigible are improved, and the incorrigible cut off. This is implied in the idea of purification, and is confirmed by the result of the refining work of the Lord, as given in the last clause of the verse. They are to become to the Lord offerers of sacrifices in righteousness. <hi type="italic">Bitsedâqâh</hi> does not refer to the nature of the sacrifices, viz., righteous sacrifices, i.e., such as correspond to the law, but to the moral character of the offerers, viz., that they will attend to the offering of sacrifice in a proper state of heart, as in Psa 4:6. היוּ מגּישׁי is a <hi type="italic">constructio periphr. </hi>to denote the permanence of the action (cf. Ewald, §168, <hi type="italic">c</hi>). The <hi type="italic">tsaqeph</hi>-<hi type="italic">qaton</hi> does not compel us to separate היוּ ליהוה (compare, on the contrary, <hi type="italic"><reference osisRef="Gen.1.6">Gen 1:6</reference></hi> for example). Then, namely when the priests offer sacrifices in righteousness again, will the sacrificing of the whole nation be pleasant to the Lord, as was the case in the olden time. The days of the olden time and years of the past are the times of Moses, or the first years of the sojourn in the desert (<reference osisRef="Jer.2.2">Jer 2:2</reference>), possibly also the times of David and of the first years of the reign of Solomon; whereas now, i.e., in the time of Malachi, the sacrifices of the nation were displeasing to God, not merely on account of the sins of the people (Mal 2:13), but chiefly on account of the badness of the sacrificing priests (Mal 1:10, Mal 1:13). Moreover, we must not infer from Mal 3:3 and Mal 3:4, that Malachi imagined that the Old Testament worship would be continued during the Messianic times; but his words are to be explained from the custom of the prophets, of using the forms of the Old Testament worship to depict the reverence for God which would characterize the new covenant.
entries.449892005d37d811af26f3aeb2b56d1d06102147: Mal 3:5-6 <div eID="gen16967" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16968" type="x-p"/> Mal 3:5. <hi type="italic">“And I will draw near to you to judgment, and will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, and against the adulterers, and against those who swear for deceit, and those who press down the wages of the hireling, the widow and the orphan, and bow down the foreigner, and fear not me, saith Jehovah of hosts.</hi> Mal 3:6. <hi type="italic">For I Jehovah, I change not; and ye sons of Israel, ye are not consumed.” </hi> The refining which the Lord will perform at His coming will not limit itself to the priests, but become a judgment upon all sinners. This judgment is threatened against those who wanted the judgment of God to come, according to Mal 2:17. To these the Lord will draw near to judgment, and rise up as a swift witness against all the wicked who do not fear Him. The word קרבתּי does not imply that the judgment announced will actually commence at once. The drawing near to judgment takes place in the day of His coming (Mal 3:2), and this is preceded by the sending of the messenger to prepare the way. The words affirm nothing as to the time of the coming, because this was not revealed to the prophet. Nor is there any intimation on this point in the word ממהר, but simply the announcement that the Lord will come with unexpected rapidity, in contrast with the murmuring of the people at the delay of judgment (Mal 2:17). ממהר answers substantially to פּתאם in Mal 3:1. God comes as a practical witness against the wicked, convicting them of their guilt by punishing them. The particular sins mentioned here are such as were grievous sins in the eye of the law, and to some extent were punishable with death. On sorcerers and adulterers see <reference osisRef="Exod.22.17">Exo 22:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.20.10">Lev 20:10</reference>; Deu 22:22. That sorcery was very common among the Jews after the captivity, is evident from such passages as <reference osisRef="Acts.8.9">Act 8:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.13.6">Act 13:6</reference>, and from Josephus, <hi type="italic">Ant.</hi> xx. 6, <hi type="italic">de bell. Jud.</hi> ii. 12, 23; and the occurrence of adultery may be inferred from the condemnation of the marriages with heathen wives in Mal 2:10-16. On false swearing compare Lev 19:12. The expression to press the wages of the labourer is unusual, since the only other passage in which עשׁק is construed with a neuter object is Mic 2:2, and in every other case it is applied to persons; for עשׁק שׂכיר compare <reference osisRef="Lev.19.13">Lev 19:13</reference> and <reference osisRef="Deut.24.14-Deut.24.15">Deu 24:14-15</reference>, to which the reproof refers. אלמנה ויתום are not genitives dependent upon שׂכר, but further objects to עשׁקי. For the fact itself compare <reference osisRef="Exod.22.21-Exod.22.23">Exo 22:21-23</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.24.17">Deu 24:17</reference>; Deu 27:19. To מטּי גר we are not to supply משׁפּט, after <reference osisRef="Deut.24.17">Deu 24:17</reference> and <reference osisRef="Deut.27.19">Deu 27:19</reference>; but הטּה is used of the person as in <reference osisRef="Amos.5.12">Amo 5:12</reference> : to bow down the stranger, i.e., to oppress him unjustly. The words, “and fear not me,” point to the source from which all these sins flowed, and refer to all the sinners mentioned before. This threat of judgment is explained in Mal 3:6 in the double clause: that Jehovah does not change, and the sons of Israel do not perish. Because Jehovah is unchangeable in His purposes, and Israel as the people of God is not to perish, therefore will God exterminate the wicked out of Israel by means of judgment, in order to refine it and shape it according to its true calling. The perfects are used to express established truths. The unchangeableness of God is implied in the name <hi type="italic">Jehovah</hi>, “who is that He is,” the absolutely independent and absolutely existing One (see at <reference osisRef="Gen.2.4">Gen 2:4</reference>). For the fact itself compare Num 23:19; <reference osisRef="1Sam.15.29">1Sa 15:29</reference>; Jam 1:17. <hi type="italic">Jehovah</hi> is in apposition to <hi type="italic">'ănı̄</hi> (I), and not a predicate in the sense of “I am Jehovah” (Luther, Hengstenberg, etc.); this is evident from the parallel ואתּם בּני יעקב (and ye, the sons of Jacob), where no one thinks of taking בני יעק (sons of Jacob) as a predicate. <hi type="italic">Kâlâh</hi>, to come to an end, to be destroyed, as the parallel passage, <reference osisRef="Jer.30.11">Jer 30:11</reference>, which floated before the prophet’s mind, clearly shows. The name “sons of Jacob” (poetical for sons of Israel) is used emphatically, denoting the true members of the people of God, who rightly bear the name of <hi type="italic">Israel</hi>. These do not perish, because their existence rests upon the promise of the unchangeable God (cf. <reference osisRef="Rom.11.28-Rom.11.29">Rom 11:28-29</reference>).
entries.6c7bf412ac26d0d7a08f5368b259e02368b74a81: Mal 3:7-9 <div eID="gen16968" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16969" type="x-p"/> After the Lord has announced to the murmuring people that He will suddenly draw near to judgment upon the wicked, He proceeds to explain the reason why He has hitherto withheld His blessing and His salvation. Mal 3:7. <hi type="italic">“From the days of your fathers ye have departed from mine ordinances, and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you, saith Jehovah of hosts; and ye say, Wherein shall we return?</hi> Mal 3:8. <hi type="italic">Dare a man indeed defraud God, that ye have defrauded me? and ye say, In what have we defrauded Thee? In the tithes and the heave-offering.</hi> Mal 3:9. <hi type="italic">Ye are cursed with the curse, and yet ye defraud me, even the whole nation.” </hi> The reason why Israel waits in vain for the judgment and the salvation dawning with it, is not to be found in God, but in the people, in the fact, that from time immemorial they have transgressed the commandments of God (see <reference osisRef="Isa.43.27">Isa 43:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.2.3">Eze 2:3</reference>; Hos 10:9). And yet they regard themselves as righteous. They reply to the call to repentance by saying, בּמּה נשׁוּב, wherein, i.e., in what particular, shall we turn? The prophet thereupon shows them their sin: they do what no man should presume to attempt - they try to defraud God in the tithe and heave-offering, namely, by either not paying them at all, or not paying them as they should into the house of God. קבע, which only occurs here and at <reference osisRef="Prov.22.23">Pro 22:23</reference>, signifies to defraud, to overreach. המּעשׂר וגתר is either an accusative of free subordination, or else we must supply the preposition ב from the question itself. On the tithe see Lev 27:30., Num 18:20., and Deu 14:22. (see also my <hi type="italic">Bibl. Ant.</hi> i. p. 337ff.); and on the heave-offering (<hi type="italic">terūmâh</hi>), the portion of his income lifted off from the rest, for the purposes of divine worship, see my <hi type="italic">Bibl. Ant.</hi> i. p. 245. And this they do, notwithstanding the fact that God has already visited them with severe punishment, viz., with the curse of barrenness and of the failure of the harvest. We may see from Mal 3:10-12, that the curse with which they were smitten consisted in this. ואתי is adversative: yet ye defraud me, and indeed the whole nation, and not merely certain individuals.
entries.ce8a5c320507bb82ea0205d715e1f8af6d4e0c43: Mal 3:10-12 <div eID="gen16969" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16970" type="x-p"/> Mal 3:10. <hi type="italic">“Bring ye all the tithe into the treasure-house, that there may be consumption in my house, and prove me now herewith, saith Jehovah of hosts, if I do not open you the sluices of heaven, and pour you out a blessing to superabundance.</hi> Mal 3:11. <hi type="italic">And I will rebuke the devourer for you, that he may not destroy the fruit of your ground; and your vine will not miscarry in the field, saith Jehovah of hosts.</hi> Mal 3:12. <hi type="italic">And all nations will call you blessed; for ye will be a land of good pleasure, saith Jehovah of hosts.” </hi> In <hi type="italic">Mal 3:10</hi> the emphasis lies upon <hi type="italic">kol</hi>: the <hi type="italic">whole</hi> of the tithe they are to bring, and not merely a portion of it, and so defraud the Lord; for the tithe was paid to Jehovah for His servants the Levites (Num 18:24). It was delivered, at least after the times of the later kings, at the sanctuary, where store-chambers were built for the purpose (cf. 2Ch 31:11.; <reference osisRef="Neh.10.38-Neh.10.39">Neh 10:38-39</reference>; <reference osisRef="Neh.12.44">Neh 12:44</reference>; <reference osisRef="Neh.13.12">Neh 13:12</reference>). <hi type="italic">Tereph</hi> signifies here food, or consumption, as in <reference osisRef="Prov.31.15">Pro 31:15</reference>; Psa 111:5. בּזאת, through this, i.e., through their giving to God what they are under obligation to give Him, they are to prove God, whether in His attitude towards them He is no longer the holy and righteous God (Mal 2:17; Mal 3:6). Then will they also learn, that He causes the promised blessing to flow in the richest abundance to those who keep His commandments. אם לא is not a particle of asseveration or oath (Koehler), but an indirect question: whether not. Opening the sluices of heaven is a figure, denoting the most copious supply of blessing, so that it flows down from heaven like a pouring rain (as in 2Ki 7:2). עד בּלי די, till there is no more need, i.e., in superabundance. This thought is individualized in Mal 3:11. Everything that could injure the fruits of the land God will take away. גּער, to rebuke practically, i.e., to avert the intention. אכל, the devourer, is here the locust, so called from its insatiable voracity. <hi type="italic">Shikkēl</hi>, to miscarry, is affirmed of the vine, when it has set a good quantity of grapes, which perish and drop off before they ripen. In consequence of this blessing, all nations will call Israel blessed (Mal 3:12), because its land will be an object of pleasure to every one (cf. Zec 7:14; Zec 8:13, Zec 8:23).
entries.c6defa5106fd528738350f36d0b210738cd146e6: Mal 3:13-15 <div eID="gen16970" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16971" type="x-p"/> The impatient murmuring of the nation. - Mal 3:13. <hi type="italic">“Your words do violence to me, saith Jehovah; and ye say, What do we converse against Thee?</hi> Mal 3:14. <hi type="italic">Ye say, It is vain to serve God; and what gain is it, that we have kept His guard, and have gone about in deep mourning before Jehovah of hosts?</hi> Mal 3:15. <hi type="italic">And now we call the proud blessed: not only have the doers of wickedness been built up, but they have also tempted God and have been saved.” </hi> After the Lord has disclosed to the people the cause of His withholding His blessing, He shows them still further, that their murmuring against Him is unjust, and that the coming day of judgment will bring to light the distinction between the wicked and those who fear God. חזק with על, to be strong over any one, does not mean to be harsh or burdensome, but to do violence to a person, to overpower him (cf. <reference osisRef="Exod.12.33">Exo 12:33</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Sam.24.4">2Sa 24:4</reference>, etc.). The niphal <hi type="italic">nidbar</hi> has a reciprocal meaning, to converse with one another (cf. <reference osisRef="Ezek.33.30">Eze 33:30</reference>). The conversations which they carry on with one another take this direction, that it is useless to serve God, because the righteous have no advantage over sinners. For שׁמר משׁמרתּו see the comm. on Gen 26:5. <hi type="italic">Hâlakh qedōrannı̄th</hi>, to go about dirty or black, either with their faces and clothes unwashed, or wrapped in black mourning costume (<hi type="italic">saq</hi>), is a sign of mourning, here of fasting, as mourning for sin (cf. <reference osisRef="Ps.35.13-Ps.35.14">Psa 35:13-14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.38.7">Psa 38:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.30.28">Job 30:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.30.1">1</reference> Maccabees 3:48). מפּני יהוה, from awe of Jehovah. The fasting, and that in its external form, they bring into prominence as a special sign of their piety, as an act of penitence, through which they make reparation for certain sins against God, by which we are not to understand the fasting prescribed for the day of atonement, but voluntary fasting, which was regarded as a special sign of piety. What is reprehensible in the state of mind expressing itself in these words, is not so much the complaint that their piety brings them no gain (for such complaints were uttered even by believing souls in their hours of temptation; cf. <reference osisRef="Ps.73.13">Psa 73:13</reference>), as the delusion that their merely outward worship, which was bad enough according to what has already been affirmed, is the genuine worship which God must acknowledge and reward. This disposition to attribute worth to the <hi type="italic">opus operatum</hi> of fasting it attacked even by Isaiah, in <reference osisRef="Isa.58.1-Isa.58.14">Isa 58:1-14</reference>; but after the captivity it continued to increase, until it reached its culminating point in Pharisaism. How thoroughly different the persons speaking here are from the believing souls under temptation, who also appeal to their righteousness when calling upon God in their trouble, is especially clear from their further words in Mal 3:15. Because God does not reward their fasting with blessing and prosperity, they begin to call the proud sinners, who have happiness and success, blessed. ועתּה is the particle of inference. The participle מאשּׁרים has the force of a <hi type="italic">futurum instans</hi> (cf. Ewald, §306, <hi type="italic">d</hi>), denoting what men prepare to do. <hi type="italic">Zēdı̄m</hi>, the haughty or proud, are the heathen, as in <reference osisRef="Isa.13.11">Isa 13:11</reference>, who are called עשׂי רשׁעה in the following clause. The next two clauses are placed in a reciprocal relation to one another by <hi type="italic">gam</hi> ... <hi type="italic">gam</hi> (cf. <reference osisRef="Jer.12.16-Jer.12.17">Jer 12:16-17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exod.1.21">Exo 1:21</reference>), and also, notwithstanding the fact that they have tempted God, are delivered when they fall into misfortune. <hi type="italic">Bâchan Elohim</hi>, to prove or test God, i.e., to call out His judgment through their wickedness.
entries.f1fcd33399cef95dc9324cafdda9d144e581eab4: Mal 3:16-18 <div eID="gen16971" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16972" type="x-p"/> With these foolish speeches the prophet proceeds in Mal 3:16. to contrast the conduct of those who fear God, pointing to the blessing which they derive from their piety. Mal 3:16. <hi type="italic">“Then those who feared Jehovah conversed with one another, and Jehovah attended and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before Him, for those who fear Jehovah and reverence His name.</hi> Mal 3:17. <hi type="italic">And they will be to me as a possession, saith Jehovah of hosts, for the day that I create, and I will spare them as a man spareth his son that serveth him.</hi> Mal 3:18. <hi type="italic">And ye will again perceive the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between him that serveth God and him that serveth Him not.” </hi>אז, <hi type="italic">then</hi>, indicates that the conversation of those who feared God had been occasioned by the words of the ungodly. The substance of this conversation is not described more minutely, but may be gathered from the context, namely, from the statement as to the attitude in which Jehovah stood towards them. We may see from this, that they strengthened themselves in their faith in Jehovah, as the holy God and just Judge who would in due time repay both the wicked and the righteous according to their deeds, and thus presented a great contrast to the great mass with their blasphemous sayings. This description of the conduct of the godly is an indirect admonition to the people, as to what their attitude towards God ought to be. What was done by those who feared Jehovah ought to be taken as a model by the whole nation which called Jehovah its God. Jehovah not only took notice of these conversations, but had them written in a book of remembrance, to reward them for them in due time. Writing in a book of remembrance recals to mind the custom of the Persians, of having the names of those who deserved well of the king entered in a book with a notice of their merits, that they might be rewarded for them at some future time (<reference osisRef="Esth.6.1">Est 6:1</reference>); but it rests upon the much older idea, that the names and actions of the righteous are written in a book before God (cf. <reference osisRef="Ps.56.9">Psa 56:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.7.10">Dan 7:10</reference>). This book was written לפניו, before Jehovah, i.e., not in His presence, but in order that it might lie before Jehovah, and remind Him of the righteous and their deeds. ליראי is a <hi type="italic">dat. com.</hi>: “for those who fear God,” i.e., for their good. חשׁב שׁם, to consider or value the name of the Lord (cf. <reference osisRef="Isa.13.17">Isa 13:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.33.8">Isa 33:8</reference>). This writing was done because the Lord would make them His own on the day of His coming, and show them mercy. <hi type="italic">Layyōm</hi>: for the day = on the day; the <hi type="italic">lamed</hi> denoting the time, as in <reference osisRef="Isa.10.3">Isa 10:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gen.21.2">Gen 21:2</reference>, etc. The day which Jehovah makes is the day of the judgment which attends His coming. <hi type="italic">Segullâh</hi> is the object, not to <hi type="italic">‛ōseh</hi>, as we might suppose according to the accents, but to <hi type="italic">hâyū</hi>: they will be my possession on the day which I create. This is evident partly from a comparison of Mal 4:3, where the words יום אשׁר אני עשׂה recur, and partly from the original passage in <reference osisRef="Exod.19.5">Exo 19:5</reference> : ye will be to me <hi type="italic">segullâh</hi>, i.e., a valued possession (see the comm.). The righteous will then be a possession for Jehovah, because on that day the glory of the children of God will first be revealed, and the Israel of God will reach the mark of its heavenly calling (see <reference osisRef="Col.3.4">Col 3:4</reference>). The Lord will spare them in the judgment as a father spares his son who serves him. The expression <hi type="italic">to spare </hi>may be explained from the contrast to the punishment of the ungodly. In Mal 3:18 the prophet bids the murmurers consider what has been said concerning the righteous, by telling them that they will then see the difference between the righteous who serve God, and the wicked who do not serve Him, that is to say, will learn that it is always profitable to serve God. שׁבתּם before ראיתם is to be taken adverbially: ye will see again. The expression “again” presupposes that the difference between those who feared God and the ungodly was to be seen before, and that the Lord had already made it manifest by former judgments. This had been the case in Egypt, where the Lord had caused such a separation to be made (<reference osisRef="Exod.11.7">Exo 11:7</reference>). The words do not imply that the persons addressed had previously stood in a different relation to this question from that in which they were standing then (Koehler). ראה בין does not mean to look in between (Hitzig), but בּין is used in the sense of a substantive, signifying that which is between the two, the difference between the two. That בּין was originally a noun is evident from the dual הבּינים in <reference osisRef="1Sam.17.4">1Sa 17:4</reference>, 1Sa 17:23.  <chapter eID="Mal.3"/> <div eID="gen16972" type="x-p"/>

entries.0faf94351970436f822654fb1ae08eb5841eb9d7:
CHAPTER 3
Malachi 3:1
1. Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, who ye delight in: behold, he shall come, saith the LORD of hosts.
1. Ecce ego mitto Angelum meum, et purgabit viam coram facie mea; et mox veniet ad templum suum Dominus, quem vos quaeritis, et Angelo foederis quem vos expetitis; ecce venit, dicit Iehova exercituum.
 
Here the Prophet does not bring comfort to the wicked slanderers previously mentioned, but asserts the constancy of his faith in opposition to their blasphemous words; as though he had said, “Though they impiously declare that they have been either deceived or forsaken by the God in whom they had hoped, yet his covenant shall not be in vain.” The design of what is announced is like that of the declaration made elsewhere,
“Though men are perfidious and false, yet God remains true, and cannot depart from his own nature.” (Numbers 23:19.)
God then does here gloriously triumph over the Jews, and alleges his own covenant in opposition to their disgraceful slanders, because their wicked murmurings could not hinder him to accomplish his promises and to perform in due time what they thought would never be done; and he adopts a demonstrative adverb in order to show the certainty of what is said.
Behold, he says, I send my messenger, who will clear the way before my face
As quoted by the Evangelists, it is “before thy face.” Jerome’s observation is, that the apostles and evangelists transferred the truth contained in passages without minding syllables and small words. — Ed.
This passage ought doubtless to be understood of John the Baptist, for Christ himself so explains it, than whom no better interpreter can be found; and since John the Baptist was the messenger of Christ, the beginning of the verse can be applied to no other person. Afterwards the Father himself speaks as we shall see: but as he who appeared in the flesh is the same God with the Father, it is no wonder that he speaks, and then that the words which follow are spoken in the person of the Father.
There is here a striking allusion to Moses, whose office it was to intercede, that God might not in his just wrath destroy the whole people; for as then the majesty of God was more than could be borne without an intercessor, so that the people through fear cried out “Speak thou to us lest we die,” (Exodus 20:19,) so also now does Malachi teach us, that there is need of an intercessor, by whom God’s wrath might be mitigated, which the Jews had extremely provoked. This office John the Baptist undertook, who prepared the Jews to hear the voice of Christ.
By saying that he would send a messenger to clear his way, he indirectly reproved the Jews, by whom many hindrances were thrown as it were in the way; as though he had said, “They prevent by the obstacles they raise up the redemption and the promised salvation to be revealed: there will therefore be the need of a messenger to clear the way.” For the Jews had introduced impediments, as though they designedly wished to resist the favor which had been prepared and promised to them. But how the Baptist performed his work by clearing the way, is evident from the fortieth chapter of Isaiah, as well as from the Gospels; and hence may be gathered what I have already said — that God by his fidelity and mercy struggled with those obstacles which the Jews had raised up to prevent the coming of Christ.
The verb פנה, rendered “purgabit” by Calvin in the sense of clearing, can hardly bear this meaning. It signifies to turn or look to a thing, and hence to provide or prepare. In this latter sense it occurs in six other places; and is rendered by the Septuagint ἑτοιμάζω, as in Genesis 24:31, and Isaiah 40:3, though here ἐπιβλέψεται, according to its primary meaning. The version of Theodoret, here is “ἐτοιμαζει — prepares.” The idea of Calvin may be said to be included; for as Henderson justly observes, “The language is borrowed from the custom of sending pioneers before an eastern monarch to cut through rocks and forests, and remove every impediment that might obstruct his course.” — Ed.
He afterwards adds, And presently shall
“Εξαίφνης — suddenly,” by the Septuagint, “statim — immediately,” by Jerome, and by some others, “unexpectedly.” The meaning is, according to some, that his coming would be soon after that of John, about six months; or, according to others, unexpectedly, as a light suddenly arising in darkness, without any previous symptom of its appearance.
The literal rendering of these two lines is the following, —
And suddenly shall he come to his temple, The Lord whom ye are seeking.
The remark of Henderson and of others on the ה before “Lord” as being emphatic, is not well founded. It is owing to the relative “whom” which follows, as it is in our language. — Ed.
come to his temple the Lord, whom ye seek. After having said that he would open a way for his favor, he now adds, come shall the Lord. He introduces here, not Jehovah, but the Lord, אדון, Adun; and hence he speaks distinctly of Christ, who is afterwards called the Angel or Messenger of the covenant. But the word אדון, Adun, commonly used for a Mediator, as in Psalm 110, and also in Daniel 9:17; where it is expressly said, “Hear, O Jehovah, for the sake of the Lord,” למען אדוני, lamon Aduni; the word is the same as here, come then shall the Lord. The reason for this mode of speaking was, because Christ was shown to them under the type which re presented him. As then the kingdom of David was a representation of the kingdom of Christ our Lord, it is no wonder that the Prophets designate him by this title, especially those who were the nearest to the time of Christ’s manifestation. But he is promised by another title, the angel or messenger of the covenant; but it means not the same here as in the first clause. He called John the Baptist at the beginning of this verse a messenger, the messenger of Jehovah; and now he calls Christ a messenger, but he is the messenger of the covenant;
“A phrase nowhere else in Scripture.” — Secker.
for it was necessary that the covenant should be confirmed by him. The title of John the Baptist was then inferior to that of Christ; for though he was God manifested in the flesh, yet this did not prevent him from being God’s minister and interpreter in order to confirm his covenant; and we know that the office of Christ consists in confirming and sealing to us the covenant of God, not only by his doctrine, but also by his blood and the sacrifice of his cross.
Malachi then promises here to the Jews both a king and a reconciler, — a king under tee title of Lord, — and a reconciler under the title of the messenger of the covenant: and we know it was the main thing in the whole doctrine of the law, that a Redeemer was to come, to reconcile the Church to Cod and to rule it.
And he says that the Mediator was sought and expected by the Jews; and through him God was to be propitious to them: but this was not said but ironically. The faithful indeed at this day have all their desires fixed on Christ, after he has been revealed in the flesh, until they shall partake at his last coming of the fruit of his death and resurrection; and under the law we know that the groaning and the sighings of the godly were towards Christ: but Malachi here, by way of contempt, checks these unreasonable charges, by which the Jews accused God, as though he had disappointed their hope and their prayers. For we have said, and the fact is evident, that God had been presumptuously and shamefully impeached by them, as though he meant not to fulfill his promises: hence the Prophet says ironically, and sharply too, that Christ was expected by the Jews, for they murmured, because God had too long deferred his coming: “O! where is the Redeemer? when will he be revealed to us?” Since then they thus pretended that they earnestly expected the coming of Christ, the Prophet upbraids them with this, and justly too, for they had expressly manifested their unbelief.
Behold, he comes, saith Jehovah of hosts
Owing to this repetition, some of the fathers, Theodoret, Eusebius, and Augustine, held that this part refers to Christ’s second coming: but the repetition is only to confirm what had been previously said, and according to the usual manner of the Prophets, contains an expansion of the former idea. A literal rendering of the whole verse would exhibit this as the real meaning, —
Behold I send my messenger, And he shall prepare the way before me: And suddenly shall he come to his temple, The Lord whom ye are seeking; Yea, the angel of the covenant, in whom ye delight, Behold, he is coming, saith Jehovah of hosts.
The four last lines exhibit an example of parallelism which often occurs. The first and the last line correspond, and so do the second and the third. — Ed.
Here he introduces the Father as the speaker, as it has been already stated; and the particle הנה, ene, behold, is used for the sake of removing every doubt; and then he confirms what he says by the authority of God. He might have asserted this in his own person as a teacher; but in order to produce an effect on the Jews by the majesty of God, he makes him the author of this prophecy. It follows —
Malachi 3:2

2. Et quis sustinebit diem adventus ejus? et quis consistet in apparitione ejus? quia ipse quasi ignis purgans, et quasi borith (vel, herba) fullonum.

               <ns0:p n="7">7 ¶ Even from the dayes of your fathers <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">We need not fix a particular time, or age wherein this Apostacy began; It is an old Apostacy that is here charged on them, and they were notoriously guilty of it.</ns0:note> ye are gone away <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Are tur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned away by the Examples, and by the corrupt Doctrines of your Fathers, and false Teachers; yea, you have voluntarily and of choice gone away.</ns0:note> from mine ordinances <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Which either directed my wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ship, or your dealings one with another, so that you have sinned greatly by polluting my Temple with your own Addi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions, or diminutions, with Idolatry, or, corrupt manner of performing my Service, and you have sinned against one ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther by Injustice, Unfaithfulness, and Cruelty, since you have gone away from my Laws, which direct the way of Righteous<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness and Equity.</ns0:note>, and have not kept <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi>

               <ns0:p n="9">9 Ye <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">O Priests, your sin, your Sacriledge, of which you are guilty hath provoked me.</ns0:note>

               <ns0:p n="10">10 Bring ye <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">If these persons spoken of, be the priests, then they are re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quired not to detain the Tithes in their own hands, but as was their duty, to bring them into the publick storehouse.                <ns0:p n="11">11 And I will rebuke <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Lay a restraint upon, or prohibit, and the prohibition shall be effectual, if God so check, no Creature is or dares be deaf to it; such a check not only quiets the unruly Sea, but can dry it up.</ns0:note> the devourer <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">All kind of devourers, the Locust, the Can<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ker-worm, Caterpillar, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> pests of those Countreys very often, though they are in mighty Armies and incredible multitudes, yet a rebuke from God will check them all at once as if they were but one.</ns0:note> for your sakes <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Not for Merit in you, but for Good to you.</ns0:note>, and he shall not <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>corrupt.</ns0:hi>

               <ns0:p n="12">12 And all nations <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">All, that are about you that know you, and see Gods dealings with you.</ns0:note> shall call you blessed <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Praise the state and condition you are in, and pronounce you to be a very happy People, whose God is the Lord, and whose Mercies come thus from God.</ns0:note>: for ye shall be a delightsome land <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Of de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lights, or desires able for its pleasantness; a Land so good man would desire it, and when purged, 'twill be a land the Lord will delight in, and give it the name <ns0:hi>Hephtsibah</ns0:hi>;</ns0:note>, saith the LORD of hosts <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ded as an assurance that it shall be according to this promise, for so much as he who is Lord of hosts hath engaged his word to do it, and his word will do it, can make all Creatures cooperate for that purpose.</ns0:note>,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 ¶ <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Job 21.14, 15.</ns0:note> Your words <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Your discourses concerning my Providences over you and others, your reasonings, censures, and verdicts, passed on your own wayes, and on the wayes of your God.</ns0:note> have been stout <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Proudly justify<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing your selves as deserving better usage from God, or insolent<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly arraigning God for his kindness to others, who in your Judgment are worse than your selves, by such words as those <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 2.17.</ns0:note> a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst me, saith the LORD: yet ye say <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">You think you have spoken nothing so proud<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly and stoutly, and challenge me to tell you wherein, or with what words you have shew'd such insolence.</ns0:note>, What have we spoken <ns0:hi>so much</ns0:hi> against thee?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 Ye <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Ye that are the children of forefathers, who had this good land given to them, and ever made fruitful while they feared and obeyed their God, you that have been well re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />warded for your obedience, or you Priests who have Tithes, Sacrifices, Offerings, and First Fruits given you for your Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vices.</ns0:note> have said <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Have thought first, and next have discoursed it, un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thankful to your God, you have Atheist like maintained it in disputes,</ns0:note>, It <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> vain to serve God <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">That all is lost Labour, no profit to God, nor any to your selves; therefore better sit still, and do nothing, than to no purpose.</ns0:note>: and what profit <ns0:hi>is it,</ns0:hi> that we have kept his <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>observa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> ordinances <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">While what they have before their eyes, is the fruit of Gods goodness, and what they want is punishment of their not doing it better; whilest a very un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />suitable observing the ordinances of God, hath so much pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fit for you, dare you say there is no profit?                   </ns0:note> mournfully <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">So the Hypocrites and Ungodly object against God, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 58.3. Yet their's, as <ns0:hi>Ahab</ns0:hi>'s, dissembled Mournings had their re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ward, and infinitely better than they deserved.</ns0:note> before the LORD of hosts?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 And now <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Or now therefore, on these false reasonings of these decei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ved ones, they proceed to further impiety, and audacious blas<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phemy.</ns0:note>

And could this be, say they, if there were a God of Judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment to call men to account, and to deal with them according to their wayes?</ns0:note>: yea, they that work wickedness are <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>built.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> set up <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Who contrive, and then work wickedness; who choose it, study it, and glory in it, as the whole of their life; are built up, are advanced to honours, and filled with Riches, and have fair probability that all this will last to them, and theirs.                   <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:215" rendition="simple:additions" />16 ¶ Then <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">When Atheism and bold contempt of God was grown so high, and was so plainly and smartly reproved by the Prophet.</ns0:note> they that feared the LORD <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Those that were truly Religious that knew Gods Judgments were a great deep, and that his wayes were as high above our wayes as Heaven above the Earth.</ns0:note>, spake often one to another <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Discoursed aright of Gods Mercy, Justice, Patience, Holiness and Wisdom in his Government, and manage of the Sons of Men; establish'd one another against the assaults of such proud contemptuous dispu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters; encouraged each other to wait for God in the way of his Judgments.
